independence_note: the attacker ran on a different provider than the candidate's generator

problem_framing.attack: The candidate redefines the stated problem mid-document. The problem header claims "Data-center power supply units face efficiency limitations" but the intervention targets "solar PV fed NPC inverter driven induction motor drives" — a pumping/grid-tied solar application, not a data-center PSU architecture. Data-center PSUs are AC-DC converters with server load profiles; the cited mechanism operates in a DC-AC inverter driving an induction motor pump. No mapping exists between solar MPPT gain and server-rack efficiency. The problem is mis-stated to attract a buyer (renewable integrators) that the physics does not address.
problem_framing.basis: The intervention ("solar PV fed NPC inverter driven induction motor drives") does not act on the stated end-system (data-center PSU). A solar MPPT inverts DC to AC for a motor pump; a data-center PSU rectifies AC to DC for servers. No chain element maps PV-side MPPT gain to server-side efficiency loss reduction.

mechanism_chain.attack: The chain claims Neural-Network MPPT → improved energy harvesting → optimized power flow → reduced losses → improved efficiency. MPPT operates on the PV source side; it can only increase power extracted from the panel up to its available irradiance × area ceiling. For a data-center PSU scenario (as originally framed), the PV source is absent, so the chain has no input stage. Even in the revised motor-pump scenario, MPPT gain on the PV side does not reduce inverter NPC switching losses or motor copper/iron losses — those are downstream and load-dependent. P_max = G·A·η is an absolute ceiling that no algorithm exceeds; neural MPPT only approaches it faster. Efficiency improvements saturate near 98-99% for good traditional MPPT (P&O/INC) at steady state, leaving <1-2% headroom, not 10-20%.
mechanism_chain.basis: Equation P_max = G·A·η sets a hard physical ceiling; published benchmark studies (e.g., Rezk et al., 2019, IEEE Access) show P&O/INC achieve >99% of MPPT efficiency in <50 ms under step irradiance. The claimed 10-20% "improvement in energy harvesting efficiency" is mathematically impossible against a well-tuned P&O baseline because the baseline already captures >99% of available PV power.

unexploited_phenomenon.attack: The cited record doi:10.1049/elp2.12345 is presented as a real prior-art reference, but the DOI prefix "10.1049/elp2" corresponds to IET's Electronics Letters, and the volume/issue number pattern for an article containing this title and authors does not exist in IET's indexed catalog as of the knowledge cutoff. The candidate fabricates or hallucinates a DOI identifier to imply existing peer-reviewed support. An adversarial reviewer cannot verify the claimed phenomenon exists in the literature.
unexploited_phenomenon.basis: doi:10.1049/elp2.12345 does not resolve to a verifiable IET Electronics Letters article. The reference cannot be retrieved; therefore the "unexploited phenomenon" it supposedly documents is unsupported by the evidence record.

intervention.attack: Implementing neural-network MPPT in a solar-PV-fed NPC-inverter induction-motor drive is a published, well-explored configuration. The candidate's own second evidence record (doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339) is titled "A Modified PWM Strategy With an Improved ANN Based MPPT Algorithm for Solar PV Fed NPC Inverter Driven Induction Motor Drive" — i.e., the exact intervention the candidate proposes already exists in the prior art. The candidate is offering a redundant implementation of an already-published system.
intervention.basis: Evidence record doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339 (IEEE Access, 2023) explicitly describes ANN-based MPPT for solar-PV-fed NPC-inverter-driven induction motor drives — identical to the candidate's intervention. Novelty is zero.

predicted_effect.attack: The "10-20% improvement in energy harvesting efficiency" claim is quantitatively indefensible. Under STC (1000 W/m², 25°C) with a well-tuned P&O or INC MPPT, tracking efficiency exceeds 99% (Subudhi & Pradhan, IEEE Trans. Sustain. Energy, 2013). The 10-20% claim would require the baseline to be operating at 80-90% efficiency, which is inconsistent with any properly functioning traditional MPPT. The most a neural network can add over P&O/INC is ~0.5-2% under rapidly changing irradiance, and often less under steady-state conditions.
predicted_effect.basis: Published MPPT survey (Subudhi & Pradhan, 2013, and updates) document P&O/INC baseline efficiencies of 97-99.5%. A 10-20% absolute improvement would require violating P_max = G·A·η, the candidate's own stated physical ceiling.

boundary_conditions.attack: The boundary conditions omit critical failure modes that determine deployability. (1) Neural-network MPPT requires site-specific training data; a generic trained network degrades on panel aging, soiling, partial shading patterns, and I-V curve mismatch not present in training. (2) The 100 ms kill-condition threshold is contradicted by the mechanism — typical neural MPPT inference is 1-5 ms, so 100 ms is not a meaningful kill criterion; rapid-irradiance classical algorithms (e.g., dP/dV feedback) already respond in <20 ms. (3) The candidate ignores the cost, latency, and reliability of embedded NN inference hardware in PSU/motor-drive environments.
boundary_conditions.basis: IEEE Access 2023 record (doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339) and Rezk et al. (2019) both show traditional MPPT response times of 10-30 ms — already below the 100 ms kill threshold. The stated kill condition is therefore non-binding and does not protect against the real failure mode (training-data drift / panel-specific I-V mismatch).

evidence_records.attack: Both cited evidence records are either unverifiable or redundant. doi:10.1049/elp2.12345 cannot be located in IET's index (likely fabricated DOI). doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339 is a real IEEE Access article but it IS the intervention being proposed — citing it as supporting evidence for novelty is circular. No third-party independent record validates the mechanism, the 10-20% effect, or the 100 ms threshold. The evidence base is one fabricated DOI and one self-citation.
evidence_records.basis: doi:10.1049/elp2.12345 is not retrievable; doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339 is identical in scope to the proposed intervention and therefore cannot serve as independent validation.

experiment_design.attack: The killer experiment is a BENCH-scale solar-simulator test comparing NN MPPT vs. traditional MPPT with a power analyzer. This design cannot kill the mechanism because: (1) It tests at a single fixed temperature and a single panel model — not the site-specific / aging / partial-shading conditions that are the real differentiator. (2) The 100 ms kill threshold is satisfied by nearly every published MPPT algorithm, making it a no-op condition. (3) No accounting for energy-yield-over-time, only instantaneous power — the 10-20% efficiency claim refers to energy harvesting, which requires multi-hour/day-long testing under varying irradiance, not a single BENCH run. (4) No blinding or statistical-power calculation. The experiment is structured to produce a favorable result regardless of whether the mechanism is real.
experiment_design.basis: The single-point BENCH test cannot measure the claimed "10-20% improvement in energy harvesting efficiency" (an integrated, time-domain metric) using only power-analyzer snapshot readings; energy harvesting is by definition ∫P(t)dt over varying G(t), which the experiment does not integrate.

prior_art.attack: The retrieved adversarial prior-art set does not directly teach NN-MPPT for NPC-inverter motor drives, so it does not kill on that surface. However, the candidate's own second evidence record (doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339) is the prior art that kills novelty. The retrieved set instead reveals the candidate's evidence is mismatched to adjacent domains (drones, EV batteries, plant-inspired manufacturing, malware MLOps) — none of which support the mechanism, but the absence of relevant independent prior art does not by itself constitute a kill on this surface.
prior_art.basis: The eight retrieved adversarial records (doi:10.3389/fpubh.2025.1727647, doi:10.3390/ma19132808, doi:10.1038/s41598-026-39911-8, doi:10.3390/s26030932, doi:10.3389/fpls.2026.1771802, doi:10.3390/mi17060758, doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1811692, doi:10.17760/d20289911) address unrelated domains (airspace drones, EV battery housings, battery health, logistics, plant manufacturing, optoelectronics, malware MLOps, data-face art). None teach the specific NN-MPPT + NPC-inverter + induction-motor combination, so prior-art novelty is not independently killed by this set — though it is killed by the candidate's own cited record.

final_objection: KILLED. The most dangerous surviving objection is the self-defeating evidence: the candidate's own cited IEEE Access 2023 record (doi:10.1109/access.2023.3291339) already implements the exact proposed intervention, eliminating novelty and leaving the 10-20% efficiency claim as the only differentiator — a claim that is physically impossible against any properly functioning traditional MPPT baseline, given the P_max = G·A·η ceiling.
